oil.summary: Crude closed a volatile session with WTI firming 1.73% to $95.73/bbl and Brent adding 0.83% to $106.49/bbl, even as RBOB gasoline sold off sharply by 3.39% — a notable divergence suggesting demand-side nervousness at the pump. The week's +8.48% WTI rally is being driven by a confluence of geopolitical flashpoints: the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire remains contested after Kyiv disputed Trump's claim, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure persist, and Strait of Hormuz disruptions continue despite Iraq reporting exports surging to 2.7 million b/d. The US-Russia diesel deal, welcomed by Deputy PM Novak as a 'positive signal,' is drawing fierce political backlash and complicating the supply narrative. On the demand side, Aramco's new Chinese JV refinery receiving its first Arab crude cargo signals incremental downstream pull. CME options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting, underpinning the medium-term floor.
drivers: Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire collapse and ongoing Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure keeping a geopolitical risk premium in Brent, with $108 cited as near-term technical target
US-Russia diesel deal generating political backlash but Novak framing it as bullish for Russian refining output, adding supply-side complexity
RBOB gasoline -3.39% on the day despite crude strength, signalling potential demand softness at the consumer level amid broader Middle East supply disruption

gas.summary: Henry Hub retreated 3.20% to $3.177/MMBtu on the day, paring some of the month's 8.87% gain, while European TTF was effectively flat on the session at €87.315/MWh after a blistering +11.83% weekly surge. The Atlantic spread remains wide and the geopolitical backdrop is firmly bullish for European gas: the Nord Stream sabotage trial opened in Germany with explosive allegations against Ukraine, and the Russia-Ukraine ceasefire that briefly offered market comfort has collapsed in credibility. On the LNG side, Taiwan committed up to $4.4 billion to the Alaska LNG megaproject, locking in 30% of output over 20 years — a significant long-term demand anchor for US exports. Meanwhile, the Iran war is reshaping Asian LNG trade flows: India's demand has dropped 1.5 million tonnes year-to-date as spot prices rose, with Oman displacing the US as India's top LNG supplier in September.
drivers: TTF holding near weekly highs (+11.83%) as Russia-Ukraine ceasefire doubts persist and the Nord Stream trial reopens pipeline security anxiety in Europe
Taiwan's $4.4 billion Alaska LNG commitment provides a structural long-term demand signal for US LNG exports, though near-term Henry Hub is softening
Iran war disrupting Middle East LNG flows: India's gas demand down 1.5 million tonnes YTD, with trade-flow shifts away from US toward Oman in Asian markets

power.summary: The power and carbon complex is under acute stress from two directions simultaneously. In Ukraine, Russian forces fired 39 ballistic missiles at the power grid on 14 October, cutting electricity to at least 600,000 people — a strike that came just four days after the Trump administration licensed Russian diesel imports, deepening questions about the coherence of US energy diplomacy. In the US, PJM spot prices breached $1,000/MWh as an unseasonable Midwest and Mid-Atlantic heat event collided with the scheduled fall plant maintenance window, creating a classic dual squeeze on capacity. EU carbon (EUA) slipped 1.15% to $82.71 on the day but remains up 2.54% on the week, with TTF's elevated level at €87.315/MWh continuing to incentivise gas-to-power switching that keeps carbon demand supported. Big Tech is also pushing back against grid upgrade cost-sharing obligations, adding regulatory uncertainty to the longer-term US infrastructure buildout.
drivers: Russian missile barrage cuts power to 600,000 Ukrainians, escalating infrastructure war and undermining any market confidence in the Trump-brokered ceasefire narrative
PJM spot prices topping $1,000/MWh as unseasonable heat collides with fall maintenance outages, highlighting US grid vulnerability heading into shoulder season
EU EUA eases 1.15% on the day but TTF's weekly surge of +11.83% continues to support gas-burn and carbon demand; Big Tech resistance to grid cost-sharing adds long-term capex uncertainty
